prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, hip-cut demi statue portrait, a four-shard stained-glass mosaic body with large legible shards, every material seam physically stepped. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to two individually finished thigh-stub tips just below her hip line, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her form comes to an end, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult American woman in Instagram glam makeup — sun-kissed skin, heavily sculpted contour and a strong highlighter on the cheekbones, bold defined brows, long fluffy false lashes, shimmery bronze eyeshadow, large eyes with bright real catchlights, plump glossy nude lips with a defined lip-liner outline, long voluminous honey-blonde waves, a confident, camera-ready smile. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. Two big gold hoops stacked on each ear.

Physique: A colossal heavy chest wider than her shoulders, a waistline that still pulls in sharply, then an enormous belly and colossal wide hips flaring out again, her body a four-shard stained-glass mosaic, each shard physically stepped from its neighbours.

Boundary (skin to material, at the collarbones): a single straight, flat line runs around the base of her neck and across both collarbones, nowhere lower, never reaching her chest — never jagged, never zigzag, a clean straight cut like a cross-section. Real skin above this straight line, the material immediately below it. At that line, the material's edge rises in a small raised step above her flesh, casting a crisp shadow.

Her whole body below the collarbones is broken into four large, clearly legible irregular shards, like a shattered, leaded stained-glass window — each shard sizeable and easy to read at a glance: one large shard of solid transparent golden-yellow citrine crystal crystal, with faint feathery inclusions and colour zoning, deep honey-gold where thickest and pale lemon at every thin edge, covering roughly her left arm and the upper-left of her torso; one large shard of carved dark wenge wood, a deep near-black wood finely striped with narrow gold-tan pinstripes, polished to a hard satin sheen, completely opaque covering roughly her right arm and the upper-right of her torso; one large shard of carved vivid sky-blue turquoise with dark matrix veining, completely opaque covering roughly her left hip and left thigh-stub; and one large shard of a glass vessel filled with clear rose-pink water holding a scattered handful of deep red rose petals drifting slowly, covering roughly her right hip and right thigh-stub. Thin, dark leaded lines run along every edge where two shards meet. At every seam where two different materials meet, one material's edge rises very slightly above its neighbour, catching a thin, crisp shadow line — this tiny physical step, repeated at every single boundary in this pattern, is what proves each piece is a truly separate object, not a flat pattern painted onto one continuous surface.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a soft cream white on one side and a deep crimson red on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: standing tall, her left hand (crystal) resting on her flared hip, her right arm held clear of her body, the hand relaxed at hip height, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: two large softboxes rake across her body from either side, so white light glances off one side and red light glances off the other, catching a crisp glint of shadow along every stepped seam, light passing straight through the crystal and vessel shards while only reflecting off the wood and stone shards. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears only. shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
